provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Int family batch. High-margin before/after trade with owner-operators; copy leans on paint versus replace, spray finish durability and kitchen downtime. No paint or finish brands. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Painting the existing boxes and doors, restaining wood cabinets, refacing with new doors and veneer, and when the boxes are too far gone and new cabinets make more sense
pageStructurePlus.why: Buyers arrive thinking they need new cabinets. A straight comparison that shows when painting is enough is what wins the cabinet painter the job.

pageStructurePlus.section: How the cabinet spray finish is built
pageStructurePlus.contains: Doors and drawer fronts removed and sprayed off site, degreasing, scuff sanding, bonding primer, grain filling on oak, the topcoat, cure time and chip resistance
pageStructurePlus.why: The fear is brush marks and peeling in a year. Showing the prep and spray process is how a refinisher justifies a higher number than a weekend painter.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Whites, greiges, greens and navies on real kitchens, two-tone islands, satin versus semi-gloss, sample doors, and how colour looks under warm and cool kitchen lights
pageStructurePlus.why: Colour is the decision that stalls cabinet jobs. A chooser with finished kitchens gets them past it and onto the calendar.

pageStructurePlus.contains: How many days the kitchen is masked, which doors are gone and when, ventilation and odour, using the fridge and sink during the job, and what pets and kids need
pageStructurePlus.why: Families picture weeks without a kitchen. Showing the real downtime, often a few days, removes the main reason they wait.

pageStructurePlus.contains: New pulls and filling old hardware holes, soft-close hinges, glass door inserts, crown moulding, under-cabinet lighting and painted island panels
pageStructurePlus.why: These add-ons raise the ticket and make the kitchen feel new. Buyers only ask for them when they see them listed.

openers.line: Your Maps listing has a phone number and good reviews for cabinet painting, but no website button. Someone deciding between painting and replacing never sees your before-and-afters.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what a cabinet buyer would land on: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site link on your listing goes to Facebook. A homeowner pricing cabinet refinishing wants to see oak-to-white kitchens side by side, not scroll past giveaways.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note their newest cabinet before-and-after there.
openers.linkLine: Your cabinet transformations, side by side: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your cabinet painting site still has a free-host banner and the quote button goes nowhere. Someone about to trust you with their whole kitchen notices that.
openers.hook: Open the site and test the quote button or form. Note what fails.
openers.linkLine: Your cabinet company, current and working: {demo-link}

openers.line: On my phone the before-and-after slider on your site doesn't move, so the best part of cabinet painting, the reveal, never shows.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Try the gallery on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: A before-and-after cabinet slider that works on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Cabinet painting is one of the few jobs you can roughly quote from three kitchen photos and a door count. There's no way to send you those right now except texting a stranger.
openers.hook: Check for any form. If quotes only happen by phone or DM, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A cabinet quote form that takes kitchen photos and door counts: {demo-link}

openers.line: That honey-oak kitchen you turned sage green is the kind of before-and-after that sells cabinet painting by itself, and it's buried under a dozen other posts.
openers.hook: Find their most dramatic before-and-after. Name the old and new colour if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your cabinet before-and-afters on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Reviewers say your cabinets look factory-sprayed and the kitchen was usable the whole time. That's the exact worry a buyer has, and it never reaches them.
openers.hook: Copy one review phrase about the finish or the downtime. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to the cabinets they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: Late winter is when sellers paint dated kitchen cabinets before spring listings. Agents send that work to whoever shows up when they search cabinet painting.
openers.hook: Use this January to March. Mention spring listings in the reply.
openers.linkLine: A cabinet page ready for the spring listing rush: {demo-link}

openers.line: People stare at their oak cabinets every night while they cook. That's when they look up cabinet painters, and voicemail means they look up the next one.
openers.hook: Call their listed number after hours. If it's voicemail only and there is no form, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A cabinet quote request that works after dinner: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring a sprayer or prep person. Someone good with a spray gun checks whether your cabinet shop looks established before they apply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A cabinet refinishing site with a careers page: {demo-link}

openers.line: You paint cabinets across {City}, but there's no page telling someone in {Neighborhood} you'll come out there. That neighbourhood plus 'cabinet painting' is what they search.
openers.hook: Find towns in their captions or reviews. Use the most affluent one.
openers.linkLine: A cabinet painting page for each town you cover: {demo-link}

openers.line: Most people who'd hire you think they need new cabinets and never ask about refinishing. A page comparing the two in plain words sends them to you instead of a cabinet showroom.
openers.hook: Check whether they ever post the paint-versus-replace comparison. If not, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A paint-or-replace cabinet page, in your words: {demo-link}

openers.line: Taking a family's cabinet doors off site is a big ask. A page that shows your insurance, how doors are labelled and when they come back answers that before they hesitate.
openers.hook: Look for any post about labelling or a spray booth. Mention it if they have one.
openers.linkLine: Insurance and the door process on one cabinet page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like agents send you a lot of pre-listing cabinet work. When an agent passes your name to a seller, the seller still searches you before calling.
openers.hook: Look for reviews mentioning a realtor or a sale. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where a realtor's cabinet referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} is the before-and-after every cabinet buyer wants to see. Right now a stranger has to dig through your feed to find it.
openers.hook: Pick their newest finished cabinet job and name the colour and the room.
openers.linkLine: That cabinet job, front and centre: {demo-link}

objections.objection: My before-and-afters on Facebook do the selling.
objections.handler: "They do, for people who already follow you. Someone searching 'cabinet painting' in {City} doesn't land on Facebook. The site puts those before-and-afters where strangers look."

objections.objection: Everyone thinks they can paint cabinets themselves.
objections.handler: "Which is why the spray process page matters. Showing degreasing, bonding primer and a sprayed finish is how you beat a weekend roller job and the regret that follows."
"Winter is when people are inside staring at their kitchens. The site goes up now and catches the pre-spring listing work."

objections.objection: I'm on a lead platform already.
objections.handler: "Shared leads go to several painters and you pay either way. Your own site sends that kitchen to one cabinet painter, you."

objections.objection: I'm a one-person shop, I can't take more work.
objections.handler: "Then the site lets you pick. Full kitchens over a single vanity, and a waitlist so good jobs don't wander off."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}: before-and-afters, a paint-or-replace page and a photo quote form. Less than a small kitchen."

email.subject: Cabinet painting site for {Business Name}

sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} cabinet demo down on Friday.

Keep it up or let it go? One word works.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, listing season is close and agents are lining up cabinet painting for spring sales. Thought of you.

The cabinet site is still ready, same price as before. {demo-link} for another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a fraction of one full kitchen of painted cabinets, never to an hourly rate.
The before-and-after gallery is the product. Price it by number of kitchens with sliders, not by page count.
A quote form that takes kitchen photos, door and drawer counts and the colour idea is the core. Quote extra fields separately.
Only quote a refacing page for shops that actually reface; most only paint and refinish.
Colour pages sell, but each one needs finished kitchens. Quote them only where the work exists.
Keep monthly add-ons modest. Most are one or two person shops.

lineItems.description: Max with many kitchens, colour and door-style filters, and paired captions on the old and new finish.

Max with refinish, reface and replace bands in their own words and a cabinet box condition checklist.
Max when the page has several finished kitchens in that colour and lighting notes.
Max with step photos from their own shop, cure-time notes and a care sheet download.
Max when each page has its own finished kitchens and a review from that town.

whatElseYouSell.name: Before-and-after cabinet shoot
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Same angle, same light, before and after. A matched cabinet shoot makes the reveal look as good online as it does in the kitchen."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, booking the 'before' at the start of their next big kitchen.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile cabinet posts
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Your Maps listing gets a fresh cabinet reveal each week, captioned with the colour and the street's town, so it never looks quieter than your Facebook."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review request when the doors go back on
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The evening the last cabinet door is rehung, the homeowner gets a text asking for a review. That's the moment they're happiest."

whatElseYouSell.name: Realtor pre-listing cabinet flyer
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A one-page sheet for agents: dated kitchen cabinets painted in days before photos, with your before-and-afters on it."

whatElseYouSell.name: Sample door kit artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Branded colour sample doors you leave in the kitchen, so your name is on the thing they hold up against the counters all week."

whatElseYouSell.name: Late-winter kitchen refresh campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A February push for 'new kitchen without the remodel' lands when people are tired of looking at oak cabinets all winter."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in December, run in February.

whatElseYouSell.name: Instagram reels from the spray booth
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Spraying a cabinet door is oddly satisfying to watch. A steady plan of booth reels sends viewers to the quote form."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, for shops with a booth.

withoutAI.route: Countertop shops whose customers keep their cabinets
withoutAI.whoPays: The countertop shop, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "People getting new quartz often keep the old cabinets and paint them. The countertop shop needs a site, and their customers need your number."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Counters and cabinet paint are the classic budget kitchen pair. Both sides refer.

withoutAI.route: Realtors and home stagers prepping listings
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Agents tell sellers to paint the kitchen cabinets before photos. A vendor page with your cabinet work on it is something they'll pay for."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Agents recommend vendors for a living and pay for pages that make them look organised.

withoutAI.route: Interior painters who don't spray cabinets
withoutAI.whoPays: The interior painter, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Wall painters get asked about cabinets all the time and pass. They need a site, and a cabinet partner to hand those kitchens to."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Painters without spray booths are natural referral partners, and they need sites too.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The hardware shop you buy pulls from sells to painters and remodelers. A site with a hardware gallery on real painted cabinets would sell more."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Hardware sells best in context, and the cabinet painter has those photos.

withoutAI.whoPays: The tile setter, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "New cabinet colour usually means a new backsplash. The tile setter you send it to needs a site with a gallery."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Same kitchen refresh, consecutive trades, both sell on the after photo.

withoutAI.route: Paint store that sells you finishes
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The paint store gets 'who can spray my cabinets?' at the counter daily. A find-a-pro page on their site answers it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Independent paint stores compete on pro relationships. Sending homeowners to pros keeps those pros buying there.

withAI.route: Cabinet colour visualiser for the paint store
withAI.pitchLine: "Shoppers photograph their kitchen and see the cabinets in three of the store's colours before buying a sample."
withAI.whyItWorks: It brings shoppers in with a colour shortlist and keeps them from buying online.

withAI.route: Listing-prep cabinet estimate tool for agents
withAI.pitchLine: "Agents snap the seller's kitchen and get a quick cabinet painting range and a painter to call before the listing photos."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agents need fast answers for sellers, and every request routes the work to one cabinet painter.

withAI.pitchLine: "The wall painter who refers your cabinets loses room quotes to slow follow-up. Same follow-up setup you have, set for them."
withAI.whyItWorks: A second build of a working tool, introduced by a client who trusts you.

withAI.pitchLine: "The stager uploads walkthrough photos and gets a draft refresh list, cabinets, paint and fixtures, to send to the seller."
withAI.whyItWorks: Stagers write that list for every house. Drafting it saves hours and routes cabinet work to one shop.

withAI.route: Hardware supplier's fit and finish helper
withAI.pitchLine: "Customers ask which pulls cover old holes and what finish works with a painted cabinet. An assistant trained on the catalogue answers."
withAI.whyItWorks: Wrong-size returns cost hardware shops. A helper that answers fit questions cuts them.

withAI.pitchLine: "Buyers see their chosen slab next to painted cabinet colours, and the countertop shop books the template visit faster."
withAI.whyItWorks: Indecision on colour pairing slows counter sales. A preview speeds both trades.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back from the spray booth
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When you're masked up in the booth, missed callers get a text asking for three kitchen photos and how many cabinet doors."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and two lines of wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Cabinet painting price estimator by door count
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter the doors, drawers and island, pick paint or stain, and see a range before booking the quote visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their price per door and drawer front, island and add-on prices, and minimum job.

softwareAI.name: Review replies that mention the cabinet colour
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each new review gets a drafted thank-you in your voice that names the colour and the kitchen. You approve it in one tap."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs ten past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Deposit and door pickup invoicing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Deposit when the cabinet doors leave the house, balance when they're rehung, each sent automatically."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their deposit rule and payment account.

softwareAI.name: Kitchen-photo cabinet colour preview
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner uploads their kitchen and sees the cabinets in sage, navy or warm white before the quote visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their most-used colours and finished kitchens to check previews against. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Door and drawer labelling tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every cabinet door gets a label code and a photo of where it hangs, so nothing goes back on the wrong box."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their labelling method and a phone in the shop.

softwareAI.name: After-hours cabinet quote line
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers evening calls, asks for door count, current finish and colour idea, and books a quote visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their calendar and questions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Spray booth and cure schedule
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every kitchen's doors booked into the booth with prep, prime, topcoat and cure days, so pickups and rehangs never collide."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their booth capacity, cure times and typical job length.

softwareAI.name: Quote builder from photos and door counts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Tick doors, drawers, panels, crown and hardware swap on a tablet, and the cabinet quote prints before you leave the kitchen."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their quote template and add-on prices.

softwareAI.name: Door counter from kitchen photos
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Upload three kitchen photos and it drafts the door, drawer and panel count for you to check before quoting."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs past quotes with photos to check counts against. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Touch-up and care reminder texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A year after the cabinets are done, the client gets a free touch-up check offer. That's how the bathroom vanity and the built-ins get booked."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past jobs with dates and their touch-up policy.

softwareAI.name: Client page with colour approval and pickup dates
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner approves the sample door colour, sees pickup and rehang dates, and stops texting to ask when the cabinets come back."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the booth schedule first.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot on paint versus replace and cure times
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'can you paint laminate cabinets' and 'how long until I can use the kitchen' at midnight, from your own rules."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their FAQ and lead time, updated monthly. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Realtor referral tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which agents sent which pre-listing cabinet jobs, so you know who to thank at the end of the season."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs a referral field on the form.

softwareAI.name: Job costing per kitchen
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See whether painted oak, stained maple or full refacing actually pays once finish, prep hours and booth time are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs finish receipts and hours for a season of cabinet jobs.

softwareAI.name: Colour page writer from finished kitchens
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each month a new colour or cabinet style page gets drafted from your finished kitchens and notes, and you sign off first."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs job notes and approval on every page. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Finish supply price sync
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When the paint store changes primer and topcoat prices, the cabinet estimator updates the same day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, after the estimator. Needs the store's price sheet.

softwareAI.name: Voice-to-quote from the kitchen walkthrough
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Say the door count, the island and the hardware swap out loud, and it drafts the cabinet quote before you leave the driveway."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their quote template and pricing. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Sample door request and delivery flow
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Undecided clients request two sample doors online, you get the order, and they get a reminder to decide by the booking date."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their sample door process and fee.

softwareAI.name: Sprayer and prep applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants say whether they've run an airless or HVLP sprayer and done cabinet prep, so you only call real candidates."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any time they post a hiring note. Needs must-haves and pay. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the cabinet estimator for every refinisher
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a door-count cabinet estimator for one painter. Every cabinet refinisher answers 'how much for my kitchen' a dozen times a week."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Owner-operators everywhere have the same question to answer, and a small monthly tool spreads across many of them.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Find-a-cabinet-pro locator for a paint distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A cabinet pro locator on the distributor's site sends homeowners to painters who buy their finishes."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors compete for pro loyalty. Sending pros jobs beats discounts.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Certified applicator portal for a coatings maker
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Applicators trained on your cabinet finish need a locator and a warranty registration flow. I've built that flow for a refinisher."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Coatings makers sell through trained applicators. A program site is their marketing.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Give member painters a cabinet page module with before-and-after sliders and a door-count form."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need benefits members use. One deal reaches many shops.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies with painting clients rarely build good cabinet sliders. License my cabinet template with sliders and the photo quote form."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies keep the client; you sell the finished cabinet module.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The refinishing franchise group, per location
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Cabinet franchise owners each need a local page with their own before-and-afters. One template, filled per owner."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract becomes many locations on the same template.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A brokerage-wide page for pre-listing kitchen refreshes, with a cabinet painter, a stager and a cleaner on fixed turnaround."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Brokerages want listings photo-ready fast, and the cabinet painter anchors the package.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Landlords repaint tired rental cabinets between tenants. A fixed-spec cabinet refresh page per portfolio makes it routine."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Managers buy repeatable fixes at set prices.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Starter pack for painters adding cabinets
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Wall painters adding a cabinet line, per pack
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Painters adding cabinet work need a quote template, a care sheet and a cabinet page. Sell them the pack your first client uses."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The pack is built once, so each sale is nearly pure margin.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Cabinet shops pool their primer and topcoat receipts, and each month they get back where finish costs are moving. Nothing goes in that a shop didn't send."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Built from contributed receipts, it never claims more than the receipts show.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A cabinet client in a new city
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "My cabinet painter in {City} gets the town to themselves. The slider-and-door-count template goes to a refinisher one city over."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse everything.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The cabinet shop with a stalled site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A cabinet site that never got its before-and-afters loaded is common. I finish it on a template that's already live."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: These owners already decided to buy.

upsellLadder.line: "Let's shoot that oak kitchen before you start, same angle after. That pair sells cabinet painting for a year."

upsellLadder.offer: Cabinet painting price estimator by door count

upsellLadder.line: "Most cabinet requests just want a number. The door-count estimator gives it before you drive out."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention jobs stalling while clients decide on a cabinet colour.

upsellLadder.line: "Last year's cabinet clients get a touch-up check. Plenty will ask about the vanity next."
